s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive swelling of the manubrium with a history of previous thyroid surgery
salient_findings: Lytic lesion replacing the manubrium on CT imaging
Follicular thyroid cells on fine-needle aspiration
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
Previous resection of a large left substernal thyroid lobe 12 years ago
Swelling of the manubrium is slightly tender
Swelling increased in size over the month prior to presentation
CT imaging shows a lytic lesion replacing the manubrium
Residual right goiter is present
Lytic lesion is in close proximity to the brachiocephalic artery and the left innominate vein
Fine-needle aspiration revealed follicular thyroid cells
Pathological examination shows thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae

shortlist.label: Follicular thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Fine-needle aspiration revealed follicular thyroid cells and pathological examination shows thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae

shortlist.label: Substernal goiter
shortlist.why_kept: History of previous substernal left hemithyroidectomy for benign goiter and presence of residual right goiter

shortlist.label: Metastatic thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic lesion replacing the manubrium and presence of follicular thyroid cells in the manubrial lesion

shortlist.label: Papillary thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible transformation from previous benign goiter and presence of thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae

shortlist.label: Hürthle cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to follicular thyroid carcinoma, with follicular thyroid cells present in the goiter and manubrial lesion

raw.rationale: The presence of a lytic lesion in the manubrium with follicular thyroid cells on fine-needle aspiration and pathological examination showing thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae, along with a history of previous thyroid surgery, supports the diagnosis of follicular thyroid carcinoma, which is known for its potential to metastasize to bone and present with distant metastases.

rejected.label: Substernal goiter
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of substernal goiter, the current presentation with a lytic lesion and follicular thyroid cells infiltrating bone trabeculae suggests a malignant process rather than a benign goiter.

rejected.label: Metastatic thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: This option is too broad and does not specify the type of thyroid carcinoma; the findings are more specifically consistent with follicular thyroid carcinoma.

rejected.label: Papillary thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: There is no mention of characteristic papillary structures or nuclear features typical of papillary thyroid carcinoma in the pathological examination.

rejected.label: Hürthle cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The fine-needle aspiration and pathological examination do not specifically mention Hürthle cells, which are characteristic of this type of carcinoma.
